summary_paraphrase: A girl who takes her teddy everywhere except school comes home to find him gone from her bed; she searches, despairs, and her mother shows her the bear drying on the washing line after a wash.

beats.function: bond shown through routines; the school rule plants the one place Teddy is left alone
Teddy is not on the bed
two wordless search spreads, from frantic to sad
Mom asks; the picture already holds the clue
Fifi cries out that Teddy is missing

characters.name: Fifi
characters.strengths: searches on her own before asking
characters.change: none of character; she learns Teddy was cared for, not lost

characters.name: Teddy
characters.relation_to_protagonist: her toy since babyhood; the lost object, not a mirror of her feeling (his face stays neutral)

characters.name: Mom
characters.relation_to_protagonist: mother; washed Teddy and solves the mystery
characters.humor_source: the plain explanation ('just a bath') deflates the drama

humor_notes: Gentle: the upside-down search under the bed, and the anticlimax that the 'missing' bear was only in the wash. The picture of the washing basin lets an attentive child guess before Fifi does.

repetition.description: Short 'Fifi does X with Teddy' sentences list the shared routines
repetition.why: a pre-reader can predict and join the pattern, and the pattern establishes what is lost

repetition.description: Teddy drawn on a blue disc (page 1) returns as a thought bubble on the wordless search spreads and as the blue speech shape
repetition.why: a visual refrain carries the longing without words

repetition.description: The final hug repeats the cover image
repetition.why: closes the book on the opening picture

notes: Two consecutive wordless spreads (6-7) carry the whole search; the text skips from 'not there' to Mom's question.
The clue (a basin of soapy water beside Mom, page 8) is shown before the text resolves it — dramatic irony for the child who looks.
The answer on page 10 is in the picture (Teddy on the washing line) at the same moment as the text.
The ending spread is wordless and echoes the cover.

strengths: a very small, real stake (a toy in the wash) told at full emotional weight
wordless search spreads let the reader do the searching
clue planted in the picture before the reveal
short sentences a 3-4 year old can follow
weaknesses: the adult solves it; Fifi's search does not lead to the answer
the setup takes four of twelve pages before anything happens

anti_patterns.note: Mom explains where Teddy is; mild, because the stake is a misunderstanding, not danger.

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Mild separation worry, resolved quickly and safely by a calm parent; no danger. Peak 4/5 on the research scale (engine 0-3 scale: 2) for the crying page; joy peak 5/5 (engine 3). Not a bedtime-framed book: night is one setup image only.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
